items.title: Sign-in with a return URL to another site redirects to Identity.API's home page instead of returning 500
covers: Expected: lands on Identity.API's home page
Expected: the other site's address is never followed
Expected: no error page is shown
items.reason: This is the exact reproduction from the ticket: before the fix the `POST /Account/Login` threw on a non-local return URL and answered `500`. The case pins the fixed contract (a `302` to `/`, never to `example.com`). It runs at e2e because Identity.API has no functional test project and the sign-in needs the real form post with its antiforgery token and cookies on the test stack.

items.title: Sign-in with a return URL to another site leaves alice signed in
items.reason: The ticket requires a signed-in session, not only the absence of the error: a fix that redirected home but dropped the sign-in cookie would pass TC-BUG-34-01 and still break the user. It is a separate case because it checks session state, which is observed through an `[Authorize]` page (`/grants`) in the same browser context on the test stack.

items.title: Sign-in with a protocol-relative return URL to another site redirects to the home page
covers: Expected: the other site's address is never followed
Expected: no error page is shown
items.reason: `//example.com/landing` starts with `/` like a local path but points to another site; it is the boundary between "a return URL on Identity.API itself" and "another site". If it were treated as local, the browser would follow it to `example.com`, which the ticket forbids. e2e for the same reasons as TC-BUG-34-01.

items.title: Sign-in with a local return URL still redirects to that Identity.API page
covers: Expected: signing in with a return URL on Identity.API itself behaves as it does today
items.reason: The fix changes the branch right after the local-URL check; the ticket requires a return URL on Identity.API itself to keep working. A regression here would strand every user who signs in from an Identity.API page. `/grants` is used because it is a real local page that only renders for a signed-in user, so one navigation proves both the redirect and the session.

items.title: Sign-in with no return URL still redirects to the home page
covers: Expected: signing in with no return URL behaves as it does today
items.reason: The ticket requires sign-in without a return URL to behave as before (redirect to `/`). The empty-URL branch sits next to the changed branch, so a reordering mistake could send it elsewhere or throw. e2e for the same reasons as TC-BUG-34-01.

items.title: Sign-in from an authorization request still returns to the authorize callback
covers: Expected: signing in with a return URL on Identity.API itself behaves as it does today (authorization request)
items.reason: Every client of the shop signs in through an OIDC authorization request whose return URL is Identity.API's own `/connect/authorize/callback`; the ticket requires such return URLs to keep working. Breaking this branch would break sign-in for the WebApp and every API token. It uses the `orderingswaggerui` implicit client that the existing stack specs already sign in with, and runs at e2e because the authorization context only exists on the running identity server.
